Use Claude in Chrome to set up Stripe products and a webhook for my DGI project at apocky.com.
Step 1: Create 5 products in Stripe
Navigate to __https://dashboard.stripe.com/products__ and create these products one at a time:
1. DGI Seeker — $9.99/month (Recurring monthly)
2. DGI Architect — $24.99/month (Recurring monthly)
3. DGI Spark Credits — $4.99 (One time)
4. DGI Blaze Credits — $14.99 (One time)
5. DGI Inferno Credits — $39.99 (One time)
After creating each product, copy its Price ID (starts with `price_`).
Step 2: Create a webhook
Navigate to __https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks__ and create a new endpoint:
* URL: `https://apocky.com/api/stripe/webhook`
* Events: `checkout.session.completed`, `invoice.payment_succeeded`, `customer.subscription.deleted`
Copy the Signing secret (starts with `whsec_`).
Step 3: Set environment variables in Vercel
Navigate to __https://vercel.com__ and go to my DGI project (apocky.com) → Settings → Environment Variables. Add these for Production:

```
STRIPE_SEEKER_PRICE_ID=<price ID from step 1>
STRIPE_ARCHITECT_PRICE_ID=<price ID from step 1>
STRIPE_SPARK_PRICE_ID=<price ID from step 1>
STRIPE_BLAZE_PRICE_ID=<price ID from step 1>
STRIPE_INFERNO_PRICE_ID=<price ID from step 1>
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<whsec from step 2>

```

Also verify that `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are already set. If not, get the Stripe secret key from __https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys__.
Step 4: Redeploy
After setting all env vars, trigger a redeployment of the project so the new variables take effect.

On mobile I have to scroll down slightly to get to the text box, make it fit to screen.

That's the classic mobile browser issue — `h-screen` uses `100vh` which includes the area behind the browser's address bar, pushing the input below the visible fold. The fix is switching to dynamic viewport height:

And a CSS fallback for any older browsers:

`h-screen` → `h-dvh`. On mobile browsers, `100vh` includes the space behind the address bar, so the bottom of your layout gets clipped. `100dvh` (dynamic viewport height) adjusts to the actual visible area as the browser chrome appears and disappears. The input should now sit right at the bottom of the visible screen without scrolling.

That should recover ~40-50px — more than enough to keep the input fully visible without scrolling.

Why are we doing fixed values and not just fixing everything within the available screen space? You can clamp everything within the window so there is no possibility of scrolling, and make the elements inside the screen clamp to relative positions instead of defined positions.

You're right — the correct fix is structural, not cosmetic. The problem is missing flex constraints: `min-h-0` on the scrollable area and `flex-shrink-0` on the fixed elements. Without those, flex children refuse to shrink below their content size and overflow the container.

And one more — `main` itself needs `min-h-0` to complete the chain:

Now the entire flex chain is properly constrained from viewport to input:

```
h-dvh + overflow-hidden          → viewport boundary, nothing escapes
  main (flex-1, min-h-0)         → fills remaining width, CAN shrink vertically
    header (flex-shrink-0)       → fixed 48px, never compressed
    content (flex-1, min-h-0)    → takes exactly what's left
      ChatPage (h-full, overflow-hidden)
        messages (flex-1, min-h-0, overflow-y-auto)  → ONLY scrollable thing
        ChatInput (flex-shrink-0)                    → pinned to bottom, never pushed out
```

The root cause was missing `min-h-0` at each flex level. CSS flexbox defaults `min-height` to `auto`, which means a flex child won't shrink below its content size — so when content exceeds the viewport, the input gets pushed past the edge instead of the messages area absorbing the overflow. Now every flex parent in the chain can shrink, and only the messages div scrolls.
